rationale: On its explicitly finite-integral domain, the Lean construction faithfully realizes expectation as the real Lebesgue integral and variance as the expectation of the squared centered variable, with correct scope, exponent, and object identity. However, the two Integrable hypotheses are absent from the selected source presentation and materially restrict applicability, so the direct implication pair is Lean⇒source: no and source⇒Lean: yes, yielding not-faithful-weaker. Adjudication is required because applicable dependency/check failures exist and the source leaves both random-variable measurability and nonintegrable boundary conventions unclear.
